definition.def: If a situation or activity involves something, that thing is a necessary part or consequence of it.
examples: Running a kitchen involves a great deal of discipline and speed. [VERB noun]
Nicky's job involves spending quite a lot of time with other people. [VERB verb-ing]

definition.def: If a situation or activity involves someone, they are taking part in it.
examples: If there was a cover-up, it involved people at the very highest levels of government. [VERB noun]
...a riot involving a hundred inmates. [VERB noun]
Detectives launched an operation involving Interpol and Nigerian police. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If you say that someone involves themselves in something, you mean that they take part in it, often in a way that is unnecessary or unwanted.
examples: I seem to have involved myself in something I don't understand. [V pron-refl + in]

definition.def: If you involve someone else in something, you get them to take part in it.
examples: Noel and I do everything together, he involves me in everything. [VERB noun + in]
Before too long he started involving me in the more confidential aspects of the job. [V n in n/-ing]

definition.def: If one thing involves you in another thing, especially something unpleasant or inconvenient, the first thing causes you to do or deal with the second.
examples: A late booking may involve you in extra cost. [VERB noun + in]
This involved me in a round trip of over 400 miles. [V n in n]
